blocks.content: The Central Vigilance Commission is the main agency for preventing corruption in the Central government.

rows: Non-Statutory Body (Derives powers from DSPE Act, 1946)
Functions under Ministry of Personnel for administration

items: CVC is a statutory body, NOT a constitutional body.
The tenure is 4 years or 65 years of age, unlike the typical 5 or 6-year terms seen in other bodies.
The selection committee includes the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, not the Rajya Sabha.
CVC exercises superintendence over the functioning of the CBI in relation to offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Set up in 1964 by an executive resolution based on the recommendations of the Santhanam Committee on Prevention of Corruption.
Granted statutory status in September 2003 through the enactment of the Central Vigilance Commission Act.
Functions as a multi-member body comprising a Central Vigilance Commissioner (Chairperson) and not more than two Vigilance Commissioners.
Members are appointed by the President on the recommendation of a committee consisting of the Prime Minister, the Minister of Home Affairs, and the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha.
Commissioners hold office for a term of four years or until attaining 65 years of age, whichever is earlier, and are ineligible for further government employment.
